conventions.convention: Dimensions are positive; 1 ≤ s ≤ n. One-based coordinate label j corresponds to library coordinate j−1, and coordinate restrictions are zero-extended.
The robust inequality holds for every h and every set S with |S| ≤ s, with 0 < ρ < 1 and τ > 0; it is not restricted to kernel vectors.
Best s-term error is the attained minimum of the omitted-coordinate ℓ1 mass over sets of cardinality at most s.
Coordinates are ordered by decreasing magnitude, with ties broken by increasing index; only the last tail block may have fewer than s coordinates, and an empty tail has zero blocks.
The dual certificate uses the sign −⟨p,y⟩−ε‖p‖2 and the constraint ‖A*p‖∞ ≤ 1; ε = 0 is allowed.

The procedure uses exact comparisons, positive proximal-call caps, sound supplied solver/checker programs, and αβ‖A‖2² < 1. With N = 0 it tests the initial state; finite certificate discovery is not guaranteed.

load_bearing.statement: For positive dimensions, 1 ≤ s ≤ n, 0 < ρ < 1 and τ > 0, ‖h_S‖2 ≤ (ρ/√s)‖h_{Sᶜ}‖1 + τ‖Ah‖2 for every h ∈ Rⁿ and every S ⊆ [n] with |S| ≤ s.

For g the indicator of the closed radius-ε ball centered at y, g*(p) = ⟨p,y⟩ + ε‖p‖2. A feasible x satisfying ‖A*p‖∞ ≤ 1 and ‖x‖1 = −⟨p,y⟩−ε‖p‖2 is a minimizer. If p ≠ 0, A*p = 0 and |⟨p,y⟩| > ε‖p‖2, the ball is disjoint from the range of A.
For m,n ≥ 1 and ε ≥ 0, if F = {z ∈ Rⁿ : ‖Az−y‖2 ≤ ε} is nonempty, then z ↦ ‖z‖1 attains a minimum on F.

For S the first s coordinates in decreasing-magnitude order with increasing-index tie breaks, every T with |T| ≤ s satisfies ‖x_T‖1 ≤ ‖x_S‖1 and ‖x_{Sᶜ}‖1 ≤ ‖x_{Tᶜ}‖1. Consequently σ_s(x)₁ = ‖x_{Sᶜ}‖1.
For n ≥ 1, 1 ≤ s ≤ n and S the first s coordinates of h in the specified decreasing-magnitude order, ‖h_{Sᶜ}‖2 ≤ ‖h_S‖2 + ‖h_{Sᶜ}‖1/√s.

Under the stated ℓ2 robust nullspace property and y = Ax† + e with ‖e‖2 ≤ ε, BPDN has a minimizer. Every minimizer satisfies ‖x̂−x†‖2 ≤ [2(1+2ρ)/(1−ρ)]σ_s(x†)₁/√s + [6τ/(1−ρ)]ε and ‖x̂−x†‖1 ≤ [2(1+ρ)/(1−ρ)]σ_s(x†)₁ + [4τ/(1−ρ)]√s ε. A procedure output marked success satisfies the same bounds.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite-dimensional ℓ1, ℓ2 and maximum norms, including the positive-dimension restriction for the maximum norm.
Coordinate pairings, squared Euclidean norms and product-coordinate estimates.
The adjoint identity in certificates and PDHG updates.
Existence and uniqueness of the Euclidean adjoint.
Certificate bounds, matrix continuity and head ℓ1-to-ℓ2 comparison.
Residual-indicator conjugate and the dual proximal input.
Coordinate splitting, monotonicity and finite matrix calculations.
Norm axioms, positive definiteness and the Euclidean metric identification.
Reverse triangle inequalities, norm comparison and continuity in the existence proof.
Properness, convexity and the closed-epigraph convention.
Extended-real convexity and the endpoint convention 0·(+∞) = 0.
Convexity of the residual ball.
The residual constraint as an extended-real indicator.
Interpreting dimensions and s as real scalars.
Positive denominators and scalar comparisons of finite block sizes.
Passing from squared coordinate estimates to norm inequalities.
The attained-minimum convention for best s-term error.
Existence of a minimum for the finite list of coordinate-tail errors.
Finiteness of the family of candidate coordinate sets.
Finiteness of the admissible subfamily of coordinate sets.
The finite-set convention used to enumerate the admissible family.
Cardinalities of supports and coordinate sets, including the empty set.
Finite enumeration by a bijection.
Writing the nonempty finite enumeration in the finite-list minimum format.
Choice-free compactness and minimum attainment on the nonempty bounded objective sublevel set.
Admissibility of the dual proximal function.
The Euclidean operator norm in the strict PDHG step-size condition.
The proximal subproblems solved by supplied programs.
Existence and uniqueness of mathematical proximal outputs; this does not supply a finite evaluator.
Exact recurrence, supplied solver/checker interface, per-call caps, status propagation and unchanged-state failure behavior.

The supplier's strict NSP and uniform margin concern exact kernel vectors only; batch 34 separately assumes the all-vector robust inequality and imports no noisy bound from those kernel results. No reverse dependency or incompatible conclusion was found.
